title: Adaptive KV-prefetch SLI prober and fallback controller dashboard buildout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an integrated observability surface and control plumbing that ties token-level SLIs to an adaptive KV-prefetch analyzer and a fallback controller. This ticket covers: (1) instrumentation hooks for KV prefetch/hit/miss at token granularity, (2) a synthetic prober that exercises sequence prefixes to estimate p50/p95/p99 token latency under varying KV hit rates, (3) a Grafana dashboard with explorable slices for model variant fallback triggers, tenant impact, and heatmaps for sequence-length cohorts, and (4) a simple fallback controller prototype that can be exercised during canary to route to quantized model variant when admission score + KV-hit anomaly crosses thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Token-level KV metrics (kv_prefetch_count, kv_hit_count, kv_miss_count) emitted with request_id and sequence_bucket tags
SLI definitions: token_latency.p99_per_cohort < 180ms for cohort=short, < 300ms for cohort=long; these stored as recording rules
Synthetic prober job producing daily traces and p99 baselines for each region and tenant tier
Grafana dashboard (resilience/kv-prefetch-fallback) with: KV-hit heatmap, token-p99 trend by cohort, fallback-trigger timeline, and tenant impact panel
Fallback controller prototype that can be toggled in console for canary traffic and exposes decision logs to /internal/fallback-decisions
Playbook documenting steps to flip fallback on, criteria to revert, and post-mortem checklist
notes: Motivation: observed tail amplification when KV hit rates dip under burst loads; current dashboards show aggregate KV hit ratio but lack tokenized correlation to tail latency and admission decisions.
We will reuse the sampling framework from ENG-551237 for tokenized timing histograms but add KV-specific tags and sequence cohorting.
This work focuses on observability + a low-risk fallback controller (no automated global rollouts). Automated rollouts are future work and will be gated behind SLO stability.
Target regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1 for initial dashboards to compare cross-region behavior. Add ap-northeast-1 in follow-up cycle.
decisions: Emit KV metrics at token boundary only for 1% sample by default; allow tenant opt-in for 100% (config via tenant flags) to limit telemetry cost
Define sequence cohorts as short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-256), long (>256) — aligns with existing runtime heuristics used in admission

Fallback triggers will be conservative: require (a) p99 token latency spike > 2x baseline AND (b) kv_miss_rate > 20% for > 2 minutes before manual/console-approved fallback can be applied during canary

Fallback controller will be implemented as a sidecar decision service that writes decisions to the decision stream; actual routing will continue to be enforced by the ingress policy layer (no direct connection modification in this ticket)
tradeoffs: Sampling vs observability cost: 1% token sampling reduces cost but may miss short-lived KV storms. We accept reduced sensitivity for stable baselining and rely on synthetic prober to catch ephemeral events.
Conservative fallback reduces false positives but increases time-to-mitigate for tenant-facing latency regressions. We make the fallback manual during initial rollout to evaluate behavior.
Instrumentation at token granularity increases trace volume; to limit storage we will aggregate into rolling histograms in the ingestion pipeline and keep raw samples for 24 hours only.
testing_plan: Unit tests for metric emission and tag hygiene in runtime agent
Integration test: synthetic prober job seeded with controlled KV miss injection (local dev harness) to validate dashboard panels and recording rules
Canary plan: enable 5% of internal tenant traffic in us-west-2 with fallback controller in 'observe' mode (decisions logged but not enforced) for 48 hours
Chaos test: simulate shard eviction and verify fallback controller surfaces decisions and dashboard shows expected correlation
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge instrumentation PR to canary branch and deploy to staging
Step 2: Run synthetic prober for 24h and validate baselines
Step 3: Deploy dashboard and recording rules to dev Grafana
Step 4: Deploy fallback controller in 'observe' mode to us-west-2 for internal traffic (5%)
Step 5: If stable, enable console toggle for manual fallback and run a 48h canary with SRE on-call
Step 6: Post-canary review and decide automated policies in follow-up ticket
risks: Telemetry cost overruns if sampling is misconfigured — mitigate with automatic sampling caps and billing alerts
False correlation between KV misses and tail latency due to client-side batching changes — mitigate with cohorting by client-version tag
Fallback-induced instability if routing layer misapplies decisions; to mitigate, fallback controller only writes decisions and does not mutate routing in this ticket
